# Stream plots {#sec-stream-plots}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
# fonts ----
library(extrafont)
library(sysfonts)
source("_common.R")
# use font
showtext::showtext_auto()
# set theme
ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_hypercolor(
    base_size = 14))
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Theme: `theme_hypercolor()`

Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_hypercolor()`, built from Generra Hypercolor shirts: a deep purple background, a magenta frame, heat changing magenta, orange, purple, blue, green, and yellow marks, and a Gill Sans title.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

<br>

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '75%'
#| out-width: '75%'
#| fig-align: right
library(ggstream)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
fads <- tibble(
  fad = c("Slap bracelets", "Hypercolor", "Koosh balls", "Scrunchies"),
  peak = c(1990.8, 1991.5, 1992.5, 1994),
  spread = c(0.4, 0.6, 1.5, 2.2),
  total = c(3000, 4000, 5000, 9000))
set.seed(1991)
fad_sales <- expand_grid(
  month = seq(as.Date("1990-01-01"), as.Date("1999-12-01"), by = "month"),
  fads) |>
  mutate(
    fad = factor(fad, levels = fads$fad),
    t = lubridate::year(month) + (lubridate::month(month) - 1) / 12,
    avg_sales = total / 12 * dnorm(t, mean = peak, sd = spread),
    sales = rpois(n(), lambda = avg_sales)) |>
  select(month, fad, avg_sales, sales)
labs_stream <- labs(
    title = "90s fads",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle =
        paste0("Monthly sales between ",
            format(min(fad_sales$month), "%Y"),
            " and ",
            format(max(fad_sales$month), "%Y")),
    x = "Month",
    y = "Sales (thousands)",
    fill = "Fad")
ggp2_stream <- ggplot(data = fad_sales,
    mapping = aes(x = month,
                  y = sales,
                  fill = fad)) +
    ggstream::geom_stream()
ggp2_stream +
    labs_stream +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          axis.text.y = element_blank())
```

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a categorical variable**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a numeric (continuous) variable**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a numeric (date) variable**

::::

## Description

Stream graphs display how a numerical variable (typically on the `y` axis) changes over time (on the `x` axis) across levels of a categorical variable. These graphs are handy if the numerical value varies wildly (or isn't always present) over the time measurement.

Categorical groups are differentiated by color layers, with the area of the layer representing the change in `y` value. In `ggplot2`, we can create stream graphs using [ggstream.](https://github.com/davidsjoberg/ggstream)

## Set up

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**PACKAGES:**
:::

Install packages.


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_stream
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
remotes::install_github("davidsjoberg/ggstream")
library(ggstream)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for data manipulation
library(tidyr) # for expand_grid()
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

The 90s were a decade of fads that showed up overnight and vanished just as fast. Slap bracelets were banned from schools, Hypercolor shirts changed color when you touched them, and Koosh balls and scrunchies were everywhere.

We'll simulate the monthly sales (in thousands) for four fads from 1990 through 1999. Each fad in `fads` gets a `peak` (the year it was most popular), a `spread` (how long it lasted, in years), and a `total` (how many it sold overall). The monthly average (`avg_sales`) follows a bell shaped curve around the peak, and `rpois()` draws the actual monthly sales. Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same `r dplyr::n_distinct(fad_sales$month)` months of sales every time you run the code below.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_stream
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
fads <- tibble(
  fad = c("Slap bracelets", "Hypercolor", "Koosh balls", "Scrunchies"), # four early 90s fads
  peak = c(1990.8, 1991.5, 1992.5, 1994), # when each fad peaked
  spread = c(0.4, 0.6, 1.5, 2.2), # how long each fad lasted (in years)
  total = c(3000, 4000, 5000, 9000) # total sales over the decade
  )
set.seed(1991) # same monthly sales every time the code runs
fad_sales <- expand_grid(
  month = seq(as.Date("1990-01-01"), as.Date("1999-12-01"), by = "month"), # 120 months
  fads # every fad in every month
  ) |>
  mutate(
    fad = factor(fad, levels = fads$fad), # keep the order above
    t = lubridate::year(month) + (lubridate::month(month) - 1) / 12, # month as a decimal year
    avg_sales = total / 12 * dnorm(t, mean = peak, sd = spread), # bell shaped rise and fall
    sales = rpois(n(), lambda = avg_sales) # monthly sales around the curve
    ) |>
  select(month, fad, avg_sales, sales)
glimpse(fad_sales)
```
:::

## Distribution

A stream plot stacks each group's values on top of one another and lets the stack flow over time. Each fad's layer has its own shape: a quick spike for fads that burned out fast, and a long, low hump for fads that hung around. Below we'll move from the monthly sales, to a picture, to the formula, and see where those shapes come from.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**COUNT IT:**
:::

Start with the first six months of Hypercolor sales in 1991.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_values_stream
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
fad_sales |>
  filter(fad == "Hypercolor", month >= as.Date("1991-01-01")) |>
  head(6)
```
:::

Sales wobble a little from month to month, but they climb toward the summer of 1991 right along with `avg_sales`. Below we total each fad's sales and find its best month.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_summary_stream
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
fad_peaks <- fad_sales |>
  group_by(fad) |>
  summarise(total_sales = sum(sales),
            best_month = month[which.max(sales)],
            best_sales = max(sales))
fad_peaks
```
:::

Scrunchies sold the most overall (`r scales::comma(fad_peaks$total_sales[fad_peaks$fad == "Scrunchies"])` thousand), but slap bracelets had the biggest single month (`r fad_peaks$best_sales[fad_peaks$fad == "Slap bracelets"]` thousand). Selling the most and peaking the highest are two different things.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DRAW IT:**
:::

The graph below draws each fad's monthly sales as points and its `avg_sales` as a line. Every fad follows the same bell shaped curve. Slap bracelets and Hypercolor have narrow, tall bells, and scrunchies have a wide, short one.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_stream
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ggplot(fad_sales, aes(x = month, color = fad)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = sales), alpha = 1 / 2, size = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = avg_sales), linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ fad, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Sales (thousands)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::

A stream plot stacks these four bells on top of each other (and centers the stack), which is why the stream bulges in the early 90s and thins out by the end of the decade.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**NAME IT:**
:::

The monthly sales are [Poisson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisson_distribution) counts, and the average for each month follows the shape of a [normal distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution) over time:

$$
\text{sales}_t \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_t), \quad \lambda_t = \frac{\text{total}}{12} \times \frac{1}{\text{spread}\sqrt{2\pi}} \, e^{-\frac{(t - \text{peak})^2}{2 \, \text{spread}^2}}
$$

Here we only borrow the normal curve for its shape (it describes *when* the sales happen, not a random variable). The area under the whole curve is the `total`, so the height of the peak is $\frac{\text{total}}{12 \times \text{spread} \sqrt{2\pi}}$. Our ten years trim the tails, so the `avg_sales` we keep add up to a little less (`r scales::comma(round(sum(fad_sales$avg_sales[fad_sales$fad == "Slap bracelets"])))` of the `r scales::comma(fads$total[1])` for slap bracelets).

Slap bracelets sold `r fads$total[1]` thousand over a spread of `r fads$spread[1]` years, so their peak is about `r round(fads$total[1] / (12 * fads$spread[1] * sqrt(2 * pi)))` thousand a month. Scrunchies sold three times as much, but spread those sales over `r fads$spread[4]` years, so their peak is only about `r round(fads$total[4] / (12 * fads$spread[4] * sqrt(2 * pi)))` thousand a month. Try changing the `spread` for scrunchies to `0.5` and watch their layer turn into a spike.

## Grammar

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**CODE:**
:::

  - Create labels with `labs()`

    - Use `paste0()` in the `subtitle` to automatically update the years when `fad_sales` changes

  - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

  - Map `month` to the `x`, `sales` to `y`, and `fad` to `fill`

  - Add the `geom_stream()` layer

  - Finally, move the legend with `theme(legend.position = "bottom")` and drop the `y` axis text with `axis.text.y = element_blank()`. The mirrored stream sits on both sides of 0, so half of those labels would show negative sales.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_stream
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
labs_stream <- labs(
    title = "90s fads",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle =
        paste0("Monthly sales between ",
            format(min(fad_sales$month), "%Y"),
            " and ",
            format(max(fad_sales$month), "%Y")),
    x = "Month",
    y = "Sales (thousands)",
    fill = "Fad")

ggp2_stream <- ggplot(data = fad_sales,
    mapping = aes(x = month,
                  y = sales,
                  fill = fad)) +
    ggstream::geom_stream()
ggp2_stream +
    labs_stream +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          axis.text.y = element_blank())
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**GRAPH:**
:::

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_stream
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_stream <- labs(
    title = "90s fads",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle =
        paste0("Monthly sales between ",
            format(min(fad_sales$month), "%Y"),
            " and ",
            format(max(fad_sales$month), "%Y")),
    x = "Month",
    y = "Sales (thousands)",
    fill = "Fad")
ggp2_stream <- ggplot(data = fad_sales,
    mapping = aes(x = month,
                  y = sales,
                  fill = fad)) +
    ggstream::geom_stream()
ggp2_stream +
    labs_stream +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          axis.text.y = element_blank())
```

## More info

The [`ggstream` package](https://github.com/davidsjoberg/ggstream) has multiple arguments for adjusting the shape and look of the categorical levels (and text labels).

### Type

  - Map `fad` to `fill` (wrapped in `forcats::fct_rev()`)

  - We can adjust the look of the graph by setting the `type` argument in `geom_stream()`

    - `type`: change type from `"mirror"` (the default) to `"proportional"`

  - Adjust colors:

    - `scale_fill_manual()`: Add colors as a named vector to `values`

  - Finally, add the `fill` to the labels and move the legend with  `theme(legend.position = "bottom")`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_stream_prp
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
fad_colors <- c("Slap bracelets" = "#FFE135",
                "Hypercolor" = "#E0218A",
                "Koosh balls" = "#2DBE60",
                "Scrunchies" = "#1F9BFF")
ggp2_stream_prp <- ggplot(data = fad_sales,
    mapping = aes(x = month,
                  y = sales,
                  fill = forcats::fct_rev(fad))) +
    ggstream::geom_stream(type = "proportional") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fad_colors)
ggp2_stream_prp +
    labs_stream +
    labs(y = "Share of sales", fill = "Fad") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
:::

The proportional stream shows each fad's *share* of the month's sales. Scrunchies take over the whole stream by the end of the decade, because their wide bell is the last one still selling.

### Sorting

To change how the categorical areas are sorted, adjust the sorting argument to either `"none"`, `"onset"`, or `"inside_out"`

  - `sorting`: set the `sorting` method to `"inside_out"` in *both* `ggstream::geom_stream()` and `ggstream::geom_stream_label()`

  - `type`: change the type to `"ridge"` in *both* `ggstream::geom_stream()` and `ggstream::geom_stream_label()`

We can also add text labels using `ggstream::geom_stream_label()`:

  - Map `fad` (wrapped in `forcats::fct_rev()`) to `label` globally

  - Inside `ggstream::geom_stream_label()`:

    - map `fad` to `color` and set the `size` to `3`

    - set `n_grid` to `1000` (the default grid of `100` points is smaller than our 120 months, which causes an error)

    - Keep the labels out of the legend with `show.legend = FALSE` (the `fill` legend stays)

Colors:

  - Use `scale_fill_manual()` to manually set the values using the named `fad_colors` vector

  - Use `scale_color_manual()` to make the labels white, except dark plum on the light yellow slap bracelets layer

  - Finally, add the `fill` to the labels and move the legend with  `theme(legend.position = "bottom")`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_stream_srt
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
ggp2_stream_srt <- ggplot(data = fad_sales,
    mapping = aes(x = month,
                  y = sales,
                  fill = forcats::fct_rev(fad),
                  label = forcats::fct_rev(fad))) +
    ggstream::geom_stream(
        type = "ridge",
        sorting = "inside_out") +
    ggstream::geom_stream_label(
        type = "ridge",
        mapping = aes(color = forcats::fct_rev(fad)),
        sorting = "inside_out",
        size = 3,
        n_grid = 1000,
        show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fad_colors) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Slap bracelets" = "#2A0A3D",
                                  "Hypercolor" = "#FDF6FF",
                                  "Koosh balls" = "#FDF6FF",
                                  "Scrunchies" = "#FDF6FF"))

ggp2_stream_srt +
    labs_stream +
    labs(fill = "Fad") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
:::
